Main.sentence: Super Bowl XLIII was an ___E:American football U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_football)___ game between the ___E:American Football Conference U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Football_Conference)___ (AFC) champions ___E:Pittsburgh Steelers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Pittsburgh_Steelers_season)___ and the ___E:National Football Conference U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_Conference)___ (NFC) champions ___E:Arizona Cardinals U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Arizona_Cardinals_season)___ to decide the ___E:National Football League U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League)___ (NFL) champion for the ___E:2008 season U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_NFL_season)___ .

The Steelers defeated the Cardinals by the score of 27–23.   The game was played on February 1, 2009,  at ___E:Raymond James Stadium U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raymond_James_Stadium)___ in ___E:Tampa, Florida U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tampa,_Florida)___ .
With this victory, the Steelers became the first team to win six Super Bowl championships.

The win was also Pittsburgh's second Super Bowl victory in four years, after winning ___E:Super Bowl XL U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XL)___ at the end of the ___E:2005 season U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_NFL_season)___ .

The Cardinals entered the game seeking their first NFL title since ___E:1947 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1947_NFL_Championship_Game)___ , the longest ___E:championship drought U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_NFL_franchise_post-season_droughts)___ in the league.

The club became an unexpected winner during the regular season, compiling a 9–7 record, and earning a spot in the playoffs with the aid of head coach ___E:Ken Whisenhunt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Whisenhunt)___ , who was the Steelers' offensive coordinator in Super Bowl XL, and the re-emergence of quarterback ___E:Kurt Warner U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner)___ , who was the ___E:Super Bowl MVP U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_Most_Valuable_Player_Award)___ in ___E:Super Bowl XXXIV U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XXXIV)___ with his former team, the ___E:St. Louis Rams U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_St._Louis_Rams)___ .

Pittsburgh jumped to a 17–7 halftime lead, aided by linebacker ___E:James Harrison U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Harrison_(American_football))___ 's Super Bowl–record 100-yard interception return for a touchdown.

Trailing 20–7 at the start of the fourth quarter, Arizona scored 16 consecutive points, including a safety that led to wide receiver ___E:Larry Fitzgerald U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_Fitzgerald)___ 's 64-yard touchdown reception, to take their first lead of the game with 2:37 remaining.

But the Steelers marched 78 yards to score on wide receiver ___E:Santonio Holmes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santonio_Holmes)___ 's 6-yard game-winning touchdown catch with 35 seconds left. Holmes, who caught nine passes for 131 yards and a touchdown, including four receptions for 73 yards on that final game-winning drive, was named ___E:Super Bowl MVP U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_Most_Valuable_Player_Award)___ .

He became the sixth wide receiver to win the award, half of whom at the time were Steelers players ( ___E:Lynn Swann U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lynn_Swann)___ and ___E:Hines Ward U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hines_Ward)___ ).

The ___E:NBC U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC)___ television network broadcast attracted an average U.S. audience of 98.7 million viewers, making it the most watched Super Bowl in history at that time and the most watched Super Bowl of the 2000s.

Many media outlets consider this one of the best Super Bowls from the 2000s, as well as one of the greatest Super Bowls of all time, due to the performance of both teams as well as its thrilling finale.

This game was ranked No. 4 on ___E:NFL Top 10 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_Top_10)___ on ___E:NFL Network U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_Network)___ for Top 10 Greatest Games of All Time and ranked No. 1 for Top 10 Super Bowls.

As of 2025 [update] , this is the Steelers' most recent Super Bowl championship, and the last title by a Pennsylvania-based NFL team until their cross-state rival ___E:Philadelphia Eagles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Philadelphia_Eagles_season)___ won ___E:Super Bowl LII U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LII)___ in 2018 and again in 2025 in ___E:Super Bowl LIX U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LIX)___ .

It was also the last time a Phoenix-based team reached the championship round of the ___E:four major North American sports leagues U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_professional_sports_leagues_in_the_United_States_and_Canada)___ until the ___E:Phoenix Suns U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoenix_Suns)___ made the NBA Finals in ___E:2021 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_NBA_Finals)___ .
This was the last game to feature famed commentator ___E:John Madden U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Madden)___ , who retired two months after the game.

Tampa was selected for the game site on May 25, 2005, beating out three other finalists: ___E:Atlanta U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_Dome)___ , ___E:Houston U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NRG_Stadium)___ , and ___E:Miami U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hard_Rock_Stadium)___ .
Super Bowl XLIII was the second Super Bowl at this venue and the fourth overall in that city.

In February 2008, the Tampa Bay Super Bowl Host Committee unveiled the Super Bowl XLIII logo, featuring an abstract representation of a football stadium, with blue and green colors representing the regional waterways and landscapes of Tampa Bay. Eight yards of playing field are shown, alluding to the game's status as the championship of the 2008 NFL season.

In a tradition starting with the ___E:Super Bowl XL U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XL)___ logo, two stars—one red, representing the AFC, and one blue, representing the NFC—are flanked on either side of the Super Bowl XLIII logo.  The tagline for Super Bowl XLIII as well as the ___E:2008 NFL season U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_NFL_season)___ is "Believe In Now".
The seeds of Super Bowl XLIII can be traced back to the end of the ___E:2006 season U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_NFL_season)___ .

After winning ___E:Super Bowl XL U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XL)___ in 2005, the ___E:Pittsburgh Steelers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_Pittsburgh_Steelers_season)___ fell to an 8–8 record the following year.  At the end of 2006, ___E:Bill Cowher U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Cowher)___ ended his 15-year tenure as their head coach, leaving with a 149–90–1 regular season record and a 12–9 record in the playoffs.

Offensive coordinator ___E:Ken Whisenhunt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Whisenhunt)___ and assistant head coach ___E:Russ Grimm U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russ_Grimm)___ were considered most likely to succeed Cowher in Pittsburgh.

Without waiting to see if he would be hired by Pittsburgh, Whisenhunt accepted the head coaching job with the Arizona Cardinals, a team that at the time held the second-longest championship drought in U.S. sports ( ___E:1947 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1947_NFL_season)___ , with only the ___E:Chicago Cubs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Cubs)___ having a longer drought, winning their last championship in 1908) and had never advanced to the Super Bowl in their franchise history.
In the 60 years since their last national championship, the team had won just one playoff game (20–7 over the Dallas Cowboys in the 1998 NFC Wild Card Game).

The Steelers then passed over Grimm and instead hired ___E:Minnesota Vikings U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Vikings)___ defensive coordinator ___E:Mike Tomlin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Tomlin)___ .

Once Tomlin was hired by the Steelers, Grimm joined Whisenhunt in Arizona in the same position as assistant head coach as he had in Pittsburgh, and the two of them began to remodel the perennial losing club into a winner like the Steelers.

Of historical note the game matched up two franchises previously merged into a single team, " ___E:Card-Pitt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Card-Pitt)___ ", for the ___E:1944 season U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1944_NFL_season)___ in response to the depleted rosters during ___E:World War II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II)___ .

Pittsburgh was going for its sixth Super Bowl win, which would place it in sole possession of the record for most Super Bowl wins, while the Cardinals were seeking their first league title since ___E:1947 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1947_NFL_Championship_Game)___ and only the second undisputed league championship in their history. (In ___E:1925 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1925_NFL_Championship_controversy)___ , the ___E:Pottsville Maroons U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pottsville_Maroons)___ (who, like Pittsburgh, were based in Pennsylvania) were fined and suspended for playing a game against the ___E:Notre Dame U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Notre_Dame_Fighting_Irish_football)___ football team in another NFL franchise's territory, which resulted in the NFL naming the Cardinals, then based in Chicago, NFL champions in their place, a decision Pottsville disputed).

It was the third Super Bowl in history to feature two pre-expansion-era (pre-1960) teams, joining ___E:Super Bowl XIV U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XIV)___ ( ___E:Steelers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1979_Pittsburgh_Steelers_season)___ vs. ___E:Los Angeles Rams U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1979_Los_Angeles_Rams_season)___ , the latter of which coincidentally also went 9–7 in the regular season) and ___E:Super Bowl XLI U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLI)___ ( ___E:Indianapolis Colts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_Indianapolis_Colts_season)___ vs. ___E:Chicago Bears U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_Chicago_Bears_season)___ ).
This game also featured the oldest franchise in the NFC playing the oldest franchise in the AFC. The Cardinals were founded in 1898 as an independent amateur team in Chicago.
The Steelers, founded in 1933 as the Pittsburgh Pirates, are one of only three AFC teams that pre-date the 1960 NFL season.

The Cardinals and Steelers played each other twice per season from 1950 through 1969, first in the ___E:American Conference U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_and_Western_Conferences_(NFL)_1933%E2%80%9369#1950–66)___ (1950–52), then in the Eastern Conference (1953–66), and finally in the ___E:Century Division U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFC_North)___ of the Eastern Conference (1967–69).

Both clubs have been owned by the same family since ___E:1933 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1933_NFL_season)___ , with ___E:Charles Bidwill U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Bidwill)___ (Arizona) buying the Cardinals and ___E:Art Rooney U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_Rooney)___ , Sr. (Pittsburgh) becoming the first owner of the Steelers; as of ___E:2025 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_NFL_season)___ , the clubs are owned by descendants ___E:Michael Bidwill U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bidwill)___ and ___E:Art Rooney II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_Rooney_II)___ .

It also was the first time that two quarterbacks who previously started for a Super Bowl winning team ( ___E:Kurt Warner U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner)___ and ___E:Ben Roethlisberger U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Roethlisberger)___ ) opposed one another since ___E:Jim Plunkett U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Plunkett)___ 's ___E:Los Angeles Raiders U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1983_Los_Angeles_Raiders_season)___ defeated ___E:Joe Theismann U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Theismann)___ 's ___E:Washington Redskins U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1983_Washington_Redskins_season)___ in ___E:Super Bowl XVIII U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XVIII)___ .

Warner started for the ___E:St. Louis Rams U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_St._Louis_Rams)___ in ___E:Super Bowl XXXIV U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XXXIV)___ and ___E:Super Bowl XXXVI U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XXXVI)___ , winning the first (aided by a heads-up defensive play by linebacker ___E:Mike Jones U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Jones_(linebacker))___ on the final play of the game) and losing the second one (the first of ___E:Tom Brady U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Brady)___ 's seven in ten attempts), while Roethlisberger was the winning quarterback in ___E:Super Bowl XL U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XL)___ .

Under Tomlin's first season as head coach, the Steelers improved to a 10–6 record in 2007.  Pittsburgh finished the 2008 season with the second best record in the AFC at 12–4, making the playoffs for the sixth time in the last eight seasons, and went on to earn their seventh Super Bowl trip in franchise history, breaking a three-way tie with the New England Patriots and Denver Broncos for second most Super Bowl appearances and most Super Bowl appearances by an AFC team.

The Steelers excelled on defense and led the NFL in fewest points (13.9) and yards (237.2) allowed per game, while also ranking second in sacks with 51.  Up front, their line was anchored by defensive end ___E:Aaron Smith U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Smith_(American_football))___ , who recorded 60 tackles and six sacks.

Behind him two of the Steelers starting linebackers ranked among the top-ten sack leaders in the NFL, ___E:LaMarr Woodley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LaMarr_Woodley)___ (11.5 sacks) and Pro Bowler/NFL Defensive Player of the Year ___E:James Harrison U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Harrison_(American_football))___ (16 sacks).
Pro Bowl linebacker ___E:James Farrior U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Farrior)___ was also a big contributor, recording 3.5 sacks and leading the team with 133 tackles.
The Steelers secondary was led by Pro Bowl safety ___E:Troy Polamalu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troy_Polamalu)___ , who ranked second in the NFL with a career-high seven interceptions.

For the fifth year in a row the Steelers offense was led by quarterback ___E:Ben Roethlisberger U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Roethlisberger)___ ,  who finished the season with 3,301 passing yards and 17 touchdowns, with 15 interceptions.

His top target was the Steelers all-time receiving leader ___E:Hines Ward U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hines_Ward)___ , who recorded his fifth 1,000-yard season with 81 receptions for 1,043 yards and seven touchdowns.

Other reliable receiving options included ___E:Santonio Holmes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santonio_Holmes)___ (55 receptions for 821 yards), ___E:Nate Washington U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nate_Washington)___ (40 receptions for 631 yards), and tight end ___E:Heath Miller U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heath_Miller)___ (48 receptions for 514 yards).

The Steelers ground game was led by two-time Pro Bowl running back ___E:Willie Parker U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Parker)___ , who had rushed for over 1,200 yards in each of his previous three seasons.

Injuries in 2008 limited him to 791 yards in 11 games, but running back ___E:Mewelde Moore U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mewelde_Moore)___ proved to be a solid replacement, rushing for 588 yards and catching 40 passes for 320 yards.

For their efforts, Tomlin won the 2008 ___E:Motorola U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motorola)___ Coach of the Year Award  and Harrison was named the 2008 ___E:GMC Sierra U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GMC_Sierra)___ Defensive Player of the Year.  The Steelers rolled into the post-season as the AFC's second seed, behind only the ___E:Tennessee Titans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee_Titans)___ , who would finish 13–3 but lose in their divisional playoff game against the ___E:Baltimore Ravens U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore_Ravens)___ .
It had been a long journey for Arizona to get to their first Super Bowl appearance.
After winning the NFL championship in 1947, it would take the team half a century (and moves to two different states) before they won another postseason game in the 1998 season.
And up to this point, they had not returned to the playoffs since then.
Under Whisenhunt's first season as head coach, the Cardinals finished with an 8–8 record ___E:in 2007 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Arizona_Cardinals_season)___ .
Arizona then started out the 2008 season strong, winning 7 of their first 10 games.

But then things fell apart as the team lost 4 of their last 6, hitting a low point with a brutal 47–7 loss to the ___E:New England Patriots U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_New_England_Patriots_season)___ in week 16. Arizona's 34–21 win over the ___E:Seattle Seahawks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Seattle_Seahawks_season)___ in the following week was just enough for them to finish with a 9–7 record and earn the #4 seed in the playoffs, where they went on to earn their first trip to the Super Bowl in franchise history, becoming only the ___E:second NFL team U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1979_Los_Angeles_Rams_season)___ to do so with nine wins up to that point (the ___E:2011 New York Giants U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_New_York_Giants_season)___ became the third, winning it all).
One reason for Arizona's success was the re-emergence of 37-year-old quarterback ___E:Kurt Warner U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner)___ .

After going undrafted and spending a few years in the ___E:Arena Football League U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arena_Football_League)___ , Warner became the ___E:St. Louis Rams U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_St._Louis_Rams)___ starting quarterback in ___E:1999 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_NFL_season)___ due to a pre-season injury of starter ___E:Trent Green U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trent_Green)___ .

He went on to lead the Rams to two Super Bowls and one Super Bowl win (in which Warner was named MVP), while also winning two ___E:NFL MVP Awards U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League_Most_Valuable_Player_Award)___ .

But in ___E:2002 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_St._Louis_Rams_season)___ , Warner's production was drastically reduced by injuries and he soon lost his starting job to ___E:Marc Bulger U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marc_Bulger)___ .

He eventually left the team to join the ___E:New York Giants U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Giants)___ , but once again he lost his starting job (replaced by ___E:Eli Manning U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eli_Manning)___ ) and signed on with the ___E:Cardinals in 2005 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_Arizona_Cardinals_season)___ .
For the third time, Warner lost his starting job due to mediocre performances and injuries.

After the season, Arizona selected ___E:Heisman Trophy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heisman_Trophy)___ winning quarterback ___E:Matt Leinart U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Leinart)___ with their first round draft pick. This, combined with another mediocre performance in the 2006 season, appeared to severely limit Warner's chances of ever being a permanent starter on the team. However, early in the 2007 season, Warner was thrust into the starting lineup to replace an injured Leinart, and by the end of the team's season, he had re-emerged as one of the top quarterbacks in the league, throwing 27 touchdown passes with a ___E:passer rating U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passer_rating)___ of 89.8.

With his starting job on the team more secure, Warner posted one of his best seasons in 2008, throwing for 4,583 yards and 30 touchdowns, with only 14 interceptions, giving him an NFC-best 96.9 rating.

His top targets were receivers ___E:Larry Fitzgerald U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_Fitzgerald)___ (96 receptions, 1,431 yards, 12 touchdowns), ___E:Anquan Boldin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anquan_Boldin)___ (89 receptions, 1,038 yards, 11 touchdowns), and ___E:Steve Breaston U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Breaston)___ (77 receptions, 1,006 yards, three touchdowns, 904 special teams return yards), who made the Cardinals the fifth team ever to feature three players with over 1,000 receiving yards.

The Cardinals ground game was led by veteran running back ___E:Edgerrin James U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgerrin_James)___ and rookie ___E:Tim Hightower U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Hightower)___ .
James led the team with 514 yards, while Hightower rushed for 399 and scored 10 touchdowns.
He was also a reliable target out of the backfield, catching 34 passes for another 237 yards.
Overall, Arizona's offense ranked fourth in yards per game (365.8) and third in scoring (422 points) in 2008.
The Cardinals defense, however, had played inconsistently during the regular season, ranking just 28th in points allowed.

Up front their line was anchored by ___E:defensive lineman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defensive_line)___ ___E:Bertrand Berry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bertrand_Berry)___ , who recorded five sacks and forced two fumbles, along with tackle ___E:Darnell Dockett U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darnell_Dockett)___ , known for his ability to blow up running plays. ___E:Linebacker U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linebacker)___ ___E:Karlos Dansby U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karlos_Dansby)___ was also a solid contributor, recording four sacks, two interceptions, and two forced fumbles, while also leading the team with 119 tackles.

The Cardinals secondary was led by rookie ___E:cornerback U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornerback)___ ___E:Dominique Rodgers-Cromartie U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominique_Rodgers-Cromartie)___ (who led the team with four interceptions) and ___E:Pro Bowl U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pro_Bowl)___ ___E:safety U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safety_(gridiron_football_position))___ ___E:Adrian Wilson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adrian_Wilson_(American_football))___ (fourth on the team in tackles, 75).

The Steelers began their Super Bowl run with a 35–24 win over the fourth-seeded ___E:San Diego Chargers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_San_Diego_Chargers_season)___ , gaining 342 yards, avoiding any turnovers, holding the ball for 36:30 (including for 14:43 in the third quarter alone, an NFL record for a single quarter), and scoring a touchdown in every quarter.
Also, Parker appeared to be fully recovered from his regular season injuries, as evidenced by his career postseason high 147-yard, two-touchdown performance against the Chargers.

The Steelers then went on to beat, for the third time in the season, their ___E:AFC North U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFC_North)___ division ___E:archrivals U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ravens%E2%80%93Steelers_rivalry)___ , the sixth-seeded ___E:Baltimore Ravens U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Baltimore_Ravens_season)___ 23–14 in the ___E:AFC Championship Game U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFC_Championship_Game)___ , holding them to 184 yards and forcing five turnovers.

The Cardinals advanced to the Super Bowl by beating the fifth-seeded ___E:Atlanta Falcons U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Atlanta_Falcons_season)___ 30–24, the second-seeded ___E:Carolina Panthers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Carolina_Panthers_season)___ , 33–13, and the sixth-seeded ___E:Philadelphia Eagles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Philadelphia_Eagles_season)___ 32–25 in the ___E:NFC Championship Game U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFC_Championship_Game)___ , winning more playoff games this season than they had in their franchise history previously.

Warner played exceptionally well in those games, throwing for a total of 661 yards and eight touchdowns, with only two interceptions, giving him a rating of 112.1. The Cardinals also got a big performance out of ___E:Larry Fitzgerald U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_Fitzgerald)___ , who caught 23 passes for a postseason record 419 yards and five touchdowns.
Meanwhile, the Cardinals' 28th-ranked defense showed major improvement in the postseason, forcing twelve turnovers in their three games.
This included five interceptions and one fumble from the Panthers' Pro Bowl quarterback ___E:Jake Delhomme U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Delhomme)___ in the divisional round.

The Cardinals became the third NFL team to advance to the Super Bowl after winning three playoff games despite winning its division; the ___E:Carolina Panthers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_Carolina_Panthers_season)___ in ___E:Super Bowl XXXVIII U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XXXVIII)___ and the ___E:Indianapolis Colts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_Indianapolis_Colts_season)___ in ___E:Super Bowl XLI U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLI)___ were the other two. In addition, they would become the first team to advance to the Super Bowl as both a division winner and a No. 4 seed. The ___E:2000 Baltimore Ravens U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Baltimore_Ravens_season)___ were the last No. 4 seed to advance to a Super Bowl before this game, as they were the No. 4 seed in the AFC when they went on to win ___E:Super Bowl XXXV U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XXXV)___ , but were a ___E:wild-card U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wild_card_(sports))___ team before the ___E:2002 realignment U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_NFL_season)___ gave each conference four divisions.

The AFC champion Steelers stayed at the ___E:InterContinental U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/InterContinental)___ Tampa and held their pre-game practices at the training facility of the ___E:University of South Florida Bulls U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Florida_Bulls_football)___ .

The NFC champion Cardinals were based at the Grand ___E:Hyatt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyatt)___ Tampa Bay and held their practices at the ___E:Tampa Bay Buccaneers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tampa_Bay_Buccaneers)___ ' training facility.
Both teams arrived in the Tampa area on Monday, January 26.

Also on January 26, the NFL announced that the Super Bowl game would be one of the safest places in the United States during game time. Personnel from over 20 different federal agencies were on site to assist in protecting players and fans.
Pittsburgh entered the game as seven-point favorites over Arizona.
Major factors for this included the view that the Steelers' defense was better than that of the Cardinals and the feeling that the AFC was an overall better conference than the NFC.
The Cardinals were the designated "home team," as was the case for all NFC champions in odd numbered Super Bowls.

Arizona wore their red jerseys, which it has done at home since moving into ___E:University of Phoenix Stadium U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Farm_Stadium)___ in ___E:2006 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_Arizona_Cardinals_season)___ after predominantly wearing their white jerseys ___E:at home U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun_Devil_Stadium)___ for their first 18 years in ___E:Arizona U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona)___ to combat the intense heat of September and October.

Seven plays later, the Cardinals reached the Pittsburgh 1-yard line with a chance to take the lead before halftime.

But with 18 seconds left, Warner's pass intended for Boldin was intercepted at the goal line by linebacker ___E:James Harrison U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Harrison_(American_football))___ , who then took off down the sideline for the then-longest play in Super Bowl history (having since been passed by ___E:Jacoby Jones U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacoby_Jones)___ ' 108-yard kickoff return in ___E:Super Bowl XLVII U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLVII)___ ), a 100-yard pick-six, increasing the Steelers' lead to 17–7 at halftime.

Harrison faked a blitz and quietly moved into coverage to pick off Warner's pass. A booth review was called to verify that Harrison had broken the plane, as he was tackled at the goal line by Breaston and wide receiver ___E:Larry Fitzgerald U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_Fitzgerald)___ , and the ruling stood.
After forcing the Cardinals to punt to start the second half, the Steelers put together another long scoring drive.

Aided by two 15-yard gains by Holmes and running back ___E:Willie Parker U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Parker)___ , as well as three personal foul penalties against the Arizona defense, including one during a field goal attempt, Pittsburgh moved the ball 79 yards in 15 plays and took 8:39 off the clock.
However, despite picking up two first downs inside the Arizona 10, they were unable to get into the end zone, forcing them to settle for Reed's 21-yard field goal to increase their lead to 20–7.

After the teams traded punts again going into the fourth quarter, Warner led the Cardinals down the field on an eight-play, 87-yard scoring drive that took 3:57 off the clock, utilizing a no huddle offense.

All eight plays of the drive were consecutive short passes by Warner, half of which were caught by Fitzgerald for a total gain of 31 yards, including a 1-yard touchdown in which Warner threw a fade pass to Fitzgerald, who made a leaping catch through tight coverage by cornerback ___E:Ike Taylor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ike_Taylor)___ .
The score cut Arizona's deficit to one possession at 20–14 with 7:33 left in the game.
On the Cardinals' next possession, they reached the Pittsburgh 26-yard line, but a holding penalty pushed them nearly out of field goal range.

Warner then threw three consecutive incompletions, and Arizona elected to punt rather than risk a 53-yard field goal attempt. ___E:Ben Graham U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Graham_(footballer))___ 's 34-yard punt pinned the Steelers back at their own 1-yard line. After being stopped for no gain on the first two plays, Roethlisberger threw a 19-yard pass to Holmes, but Steelers center ___E:Justin Hartwig U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Hartwig)___ was flagged for offensive holding in the end zone, which not only nullified the catch, but gave the Cardinals a ___E:safety U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safety_(gridiron_football_score))___ , cutting the Steelers' lead to 20–16 and forcing them to punt the ball away. Pittsburgh coach ___E:Mike Tomlin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Tomlin)___ later stated that giving up the safety didn't faze him, as it did not change how his team called plays for the rest of the game on either defense or offense.
Taking over on their own 36-yard line after the free kick, Arizona took two plays to score, as Warner threw a pass to Fitzgerald on a post route.

Fitzgerald caught the ball without breaking stride and took off down the middle of the field past the Steelers' secondary for a 64-yard touchdown reception, giving Arizona their first lead of the game, 23–20.
With a chance to mount a game-tying/winning drive, Pittsburgh got the ball back on their own 22-yard line with 2:37 left in the game and two timeouts remaining.
On the first play, a holding penalty pushed them back to their own 12. Roethlisberger then completed a pass to Holmes for 14 yards.
After an incompletion, Roethlisberger threw it to Holmes again for 13 yards.

An 11-yard reception by wide receiver ___E:Nate Washington U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nate_Washington)___ followed, and a 4-yard run by Roethlisberger forced the Steelers to burn their second timeout of the half. On the very next play, he completed a pass to Holmes, who took it 40 yards to the Cardinals' 6-yard line after safety ___E:Aaron Francisco U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Francisco)___ tripped.
Two plays later, Roethlisberger found running back ___E:Mewelde Moore U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mewelde_Moore)___ covered in the flat, then Ward covered.
He looked and then threw to Holmes, who ran a flag route in the right corner.

Holmes caught the pass in the back corner of the end zone for a 6-yard touchdown reception, managing to keep both feet in bounds while landing on his toes before falling out of bounds. "My feet never left the ground," said Holmes. "All I did was extend my arms and use my toes as an extension to catch up to the ball."  After a booth review, the touchdown stood and put the Steelers back in front with a 27–23 lead and 35 seconds remaining.

Following the ensuing kickoff, Warner completed a 20-yard pass to Fitzgerald and a 13-yard pass to running back ___E:J. J. Arrington U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._J._Arrington)___ , moving the ball to the Steelers 44. Many viewers assumed that the play had not been reviewed for a possible incomplete pass, but NFL Head of Officiating ___E:Mike Pereira U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pereira)___ later explained that it actually was reviewed, unnoticed by the public: "We confirmed it was a fumble.

In Super Bowl XLIII, Arizona and Pittsburgh combined for the fewest rushing attempts (38) and the fewest rushing yards (91) in Super Bowl history.
The Cardinals outgained the Steelers in both passing yards (374 to 234) and total yards (407 to 292), but were flagged for 11 penalties for 106 yards.

Arizona's ___E:safety U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safety_(gridiron_football_score))___ in the fourth quarter was only the sixth one scored in Super Bowl history and the first since ___E:Super Bowl XXV U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XXV)___ .
Warner completed 31 of 43 passes for 377 yards and three touchdowns, with one interception.
His 377 yards was the second-most in Super Bowl history behind his own record of 414 yards in ___E:Super Bowl XXXIV U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XXXIV)___ .

Eight years later at ___E:Super Bowl LI U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LI)___ , ___E:Tom Brady U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Brady)___ would break ___E:Kurt Warner U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Warner)___ 's record with 466 yards.
Warner passed ___E:Joe Montana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Montana)___ for most career yards in Super Bowl history with 1,156 (Montana threw for 1,142 yards in four games).
Brady ultimately reached 2,071 yards in seven Super Bowls.

Warner became the fifth quarterback in Super Bowl history to throw three touchdown passes in defeat (the others being ___E:Roger Staubach U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Staubach)___ , ___E:Brett Favre U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brett_Favre)___ , ___E:Jake Delhomme U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Delhomme)___ , and ___E:Donovan McNabb U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donovan_McNabb)___ ).

He also became the first quarterback in Super Bowl history to have a pass intercepted and returned for a touchdown in two different Super Bowls and is also the second quarterback to throw a fourth-quarter touchdown in three different Super Bowls ( ___E:Terry Bradshaw U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terry_Bradshaw)___ threw a fourth-quarter touchdown in all four of his Super Bowls).
Warner's top target was Fitzgerald, who caught seven passes for 127 yards and two touchdowns.
Fitzgerald set a single-postseason record with seven touchdown receptions, passing ___E:Jerry Rice U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Rice)___ , who had six in the 1988 postseason.

Fitzgerald as well as Holmes each had 100 yards receiving, marking the fourth time in Super Bowl history, one player from each team had over 100 yards in a Super Bowl. ___E:Michael Irvin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Irvin)___ and ___E:Andre Reed U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andre_Reed)___ were the first in ___E:Super Bowl XXVII U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XXVII)___ , followed by ___E:Deion Branch U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deion_Branch)___ and ___E:Muhsin Muhammad U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muhsin_Muhammad)___ in ___E:Super Bowl XXXVIII U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XXXVIII)___ and Branch again a year later along with ___E:Terrell Owens U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terrell_Owens)___ in ___E:Super Bowl XXXIX U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XXXIX)___ .
Roethlisberger completed 21 of 30 passes for 256 yards and a touchdown, with one interception.

Woodley had two sacks and a forced fumble, thus he continued setting NFL play-off records for consecutive multiple sack games by a player with 4. Arizona defensive tackle ___E:Darnell Dockett U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darnell_Dockett)___ had all of Arizona's three sacks, tying the ___E:Super Bowl U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl)___ record set by ___E:Reggie White U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggie_White)___ in ___E:Super Bowl XXXI U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XXXI)___ .
Harrison's 100-yard interception return is still the longest interception return in Super Bowl history.
With this victory, the Steelers became the first team to win three Super Bowls in the same state.
